dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise.
Hi, Denise. Um, I have a tree down on my fence. From the storm that ended Saturday. I'm not totally sure who I'm supposed to call about it.
Okay, sorry to hear that. Let me get a little more. Is the tree in your yard, or is it coming from the street or somebody else's property?

Good question. I think it's from the neighbor's side, actually. A big limb, well, most of the tree really, came over and flattened about twelve feet of fence. So that's fun. [pause] Sorry, I'm writing out a lesson plan while I'm on hold with the world here. I tutor math on weekends and I'm trying to get fractions done before I forget my own name.
No, you're fine. So do you know if the tree was on private property or city property, like the sidewalk strip or a street tree?

It's not on the street. It's in the back lot line, behind the houses. So private, I'd guess. But I don't know if the city handles it, or the owner, or if it's the electric company. There's a wire kind of near it. I can't tell if it's touching.

Okay, that last part matters. If there's a wire that might be on it or near it, don't go near it, and call the electric utility first and tell them there's a tree on or near a line. They'll treat that as a safety thing. Is the wire down, sagging, anything like that?
Sagging a little, maybe. I'm not a wire expert. I'm a fractions expert. So I'll stay inside, I guess.

Stay away from the fence and the yard back there, yes. Now, for the tree itself. City crews take care of trees in the street, the right of way, and city property. A tree on private land is generally the property owner's responsibility, so that'd be your neighbor, and the cleanup of it. Your fence damage you'd probably take up with them or with your homeowner's insurance.
Okay. So the city won't come out for a tree in somebody's back yard.
Not usually, unless it's blocking a public road or sidewalk or it's on city land. If you want, I can have someone take a look at it to confirm whose it is. What's the address?
49 Admiral Kalbfus Road. North End.
Got it, 49 Admiral Kalbfus. Is any of it sticking out over the road or a sidewalk?
No, nothing like that. Just my fence and a corner of my shed roof, which I'm trying not to think about.
Understood. I'll put a note in for a crew to check the property line, but I'd still call the utility today about the wire. Do you want me to have someone call you back on this number?
Sure. It's 401-555-0196. That's my cell.
Great, 401-555-0196. I'll note that it's a private tree with a possible wire issue. And take photos of the damage from a safe distance, for insurance and for talking to your neighbor.
Photos, yes. I can do that from the kitchen window. Okay, thanks, Denise. I'll call the electric company now and then go back to my fractions.
Sounds good. Stay safe, and hang in there.
Thanks. Bye.
